lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Build a Quiz Program
lesson.summary: Predict, build and improve a short program that asks and answers a quiz question.
learning_objectives: Build a program with several sprites

standards.text: Create and debug simple programs; use logical reasoning to predict the behaviour of simple programs
Debug errors in an algorithm or program

success_criteria: I can predict the outcome of a sequence
I can build a quiz with two sprites
I can find a bug and improve my program
lesson.real_life: Making a quiz for the family about Eid, flags or buses.

options.text: A character a program can move

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do we build and improve a program?
blocks.say: Today we build a quiz program. Zainab wants to ask a question about a flag.

blocks.alt: The green and white flag of Pakistan with a crescent and star, flying in front of mountains
blocks.caption: The flag of Pakistan. Zainab's quiz is about its colours.
blocks.credit: Photo by Burhan Ahmad on Unsplash
blocks.say: This is the flag of Pakistan. Zainab's quiz asks about the colours of this flag.

blocks.markdown: A **sequence** is steps in order. The **outcome** is what happens when it runs.
blocks.say: A program is a sequence of blocks. When it runs, something happens. That is the outcome.

scenes.caption: Read the blocks.
scenes.say: Zainab reads the blocks. Ask a question. Wait. Say the answer.

scenes.caption: Predict.
scenes.say: She predicts: the sprite will ask, then wait, then answer.

scenes.caption: Run and check.
scenes.say: She runs it. The outcome matches her prediction.

question.hint: It comes after you press run.
question.explanation: The outcome is what the program does.

options.text: What happens when a program runs

blocks.markdown: Different blocks can give the same **outcome**.
blocks.say: Two programs can have the same outcome. One uses a loop. One uses extra blocks. Both reach the answer.

scenes.caption: Program A.
scenes.say: Program A has one block that says the flag is green and white.

scenes.caption: Program B.
scenes.say: Program B has two blocks. One says green. One says white.

scenes.caption: Same outcome.
scenes.say: Both programs tell us the same thing. There is more than one way.

question.prompt: Two different programs can have the same outcome.
question.explanation: Different blocks can reach the same outcome.

blocks.title: Zainab's flag quiz
blocks.transcript: Zainab wants to make a quiz about the flag of Pakistan. First she draws a design. Two sprites will talk. She predicts: ask, wait, answer. That is the outcome. She runs it. The teacher asks the question. No answer comes. There is a bug. She adds a say block to the answer sprite. Now the cat says, Green and white! Zainab shares the quiz and asks for kind feedback.
blocks.caption: Zainab builds a flag quiz, finds a bug and fixes it.

points: An outcome is what happens when a program runs
Different programs can have the same outcome
blocks.say: Let us remember. Read, predict, then run. There can be more than one way.

blocks.title: Build a quiz
materials: A tablet with a blocks coding app
instructions: Add two sprites. Give each some blocks.
Make the first one ask a question.
Make the second one answer. Run it and check.
blocks.say: Now you try. Ask a grown-up to open a blocks program on a tablet.

question.explanation: The answer comes after the question.

blocks.say: Let us remember. A quiz needs a question and an answer. Sprites take turns.

blocks.markdown: A **bug** is a mistake in a program.
blocks.say: Zainab runs her quiz. The teacher asks the question. But the answer never appears.

scenes.caption: No answer.
scenes.say: She runs the quiz. The teacher asks. Nothing answers.

scenes.caption: Missing block.
scenes.say: She looks at the answer sprite. It has no say block.

scenes.caption: Fixed.
scenes.say: She adds the say block. Now the quiz works.

question.prompt: The answer sprite does not speak. What could be missing?
question.explanation: Without a say block, it cannot speak.

blocks.say: Fix one thing at a time. Then run it again. Checking helps us find more bugs.

blocks.markdown: Play the memory game. Then check the order.
blocks.say: First a memory game. Then spot the wrong order.

question.prompt: The quiz is muddled. Put the blocks in the right order.
question.explanation: A quiz asks, waits and then answers.

points: A bug is a mistake in a program

blocks.say: Let us remember. Bugs are mistakes. Fix, then test again.

blocks.markdown: **Design** first. Draw the sprites and what they say.
blocks.say: Zainab wants a quiz about Eid. First she draws a design on paper.
She draws a question sprite and an answer sprite. She writes what each will say.

blocks.title: Design a quiz
instructions: Draw two sprites. Write the question for the first.
Write the answer for the second.
Draw the order the blocks will go in.
blocks.say: A design helps her remember what to build. It also helps a friend understand.

blocks.alt: A single yellow hot air balloon high in a clear blue sky
blocks.caption: A balloon to celebrate a finished quiz.
blocks.credit: Photo by Waldemar Brandt on Unsplash
blocks.say: She checks the design with her mum. Then she is ready to build.

blocks.markdown: **Evaluate** means to check how good something is.
blocks.say: A friend tries the quiz. They say the answer is too quick. Zainab adds a wait block.

scenes.caption: A friend plays.
scenes.say: A friend plays the quiz. They find it fun but too fast.

scenes.caption: Add a wait.
scenes.say: Zainab adds a wait block so the answer appears later.

scenes.caption: Better.
scenes.say: The quiz is better now. She shares it with kind words.
